inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares (214.2M; cover count 213.32M at 2026-07-29). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. TROW is a funded repurchaser (H1-26 buybacks $500.8M, FY25 $620.9M), so the flat count is being paid for, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, stock-based compensation expense $216.9M (H1-26 $89.8M = 2.4% of revenue). Shares withheld for taxes on restricted-stock vesting are immaterial (2,709 shares in Q2-26) and run through the repurchase line, so no separate equity-award-tax add.
inputs.wacc_rationale: No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. USD build: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.15 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.0%. TROW's earnings are a levered claim on equity markets (fees on AUM), so a sub-market rate would be wrong; risk is charged once -- the same 10% in every scenario, with market-drawdown and outflow risk carried in the bear flows, not in a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is already inside operating expenses, hence inside the EBITDA margin. Lease liabilities ($429.4M at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment, no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are built from non-GAAP (adjusted) operating income, which excludes consolidated sponsored investment products (CSIPs), so they are attributable-only; the $1,009.3M redeemable NCI belongs to third-party holders of CSIPs and is excluded by using only TROW's attributable interest in those products in the bridge. Permanent-equity NCI ($161.0M = $11,163.5M total equity less $11,002.5M attributable) is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF. The dcf-methods routing table has no asset-manager row; TROW is an asset-light, debt-free fee business (90%+ of revenue is advisory fees on AUM, capex ~3.6% of revenue), i.e. an operating company whose value is a stream of free cash flow -- not a bank (no deposits, no balance-sheet lending), not an insurer, not a holdco. Owner-FCF + the adaptations for non-operating assets (matching-asset rule) and NCI is the right route. FCFE-at-CoE would give the same answer here because there is no debt. ANCHORS: FY0 revenue FY2025 $7,314.8M; non-GAAP opex FY25 $4,666.5M -> adjusted operating income $2,648M (36.2%); + SBC $216.9M + underlying PP&E/software D&A $278.5M ($405.8M reported less $127.3M accelerated depreciation in the restructuring) = adjusted EBITDA ~$3,144M (43.0%). H1-26 adjusted operating margin 37.4% (net revenue $3,764.4M less adjusted opex $2,358.4M). FY26 guidance: adjusted opex +4-7% on the ~$4.6B base; with revenue ~$7.69B (H1 actual + H2 at the record $1.893T June AUM) that implies ~36% adjusted operating margin, ~42.3% adjusted EBITDA margin -- the FY26 base margin. Reported consolidated FCF ($1,479.2M FY25) is polluted by CSIP trading flows (-$1,002.7M), so reported_fcf uses the company's 'operating activities attributable to T. Rowe Price Group' $2,489.5M less capex $274.2M = $2,215.3M; owner FCF = 2,215.3 - 216.9 SBC - 176.6 income on cash & discretionary investments = $1,821.8M. Acquisition amortization and OHA retention-arrangement charges are excluded from adjusted opex; the retention arrangements roll off over 2026-27 and are replaced by OHA's April-2026 evergreen partner comp plan, which runs through opex and so is inside the margin. EQUITY BRIDGE (2026-06-30 10-Q liquidity table, attributable only): cash $3,234.3M + discretionary investments $1,158.0M carried as 'cash'; seed capital, affiliated private funds, affiliated CLOs and UTI/other investments added in equity_bridge; seasonal accrued-bonus build deducted; investments hedging deferred-comp liabilities ($1,378.0M) excluded together with the matching liability ($1,268.5M). All investment income is outside the flows (adjusted operating income excludes it and interest_income is stripped), so the matching-asset rule holds. Net bridge ~$30/share.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (7.4%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (3.3%) and EPS 5yr CAGR (-1.7%). Book value grows from retained earnings plus mark-to-market gains on seed and discretionary investments, not from the fee franchise, so it overstates the operating growth rate; revenue CAGR is selected. FY20->FY25 spans the FY21 market peak (revenue $7.67B, EPS $13.25), which is why 5yr EPS is negative while 3yr (from the FY22 trough) is +11%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are not reported: consolidated FCF is distorted by CSIP trading flows in every year (FY16-17 OCF near zero, FY25 -$1.0B CSIP drag), and the attributable-OCF series is only disclosed for the latest two-three years. Attributable owner FCF FY24 ~ (2,313.9 - 423.4 - 247.3 - 143.4) = $1,500M vs FY25 $1,822M. SBC has FALLEN as a share of revenue (3.9% FY22 -> 3.0% FY25 -> 2.4% H1-26), so the SBC-adjusted series is not growing slower than the reported one. Revenue 10yr CAGR includes the Dec-2021 OHA acquisition.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +5% is mostly booked: H1 +7.9% and H2 at the record $1.893T June AUM. Thereafter ~2%/yr = market appreciation ~6% less net outflows ~2-3% of AUM less fee-rate compression ~1-1.5%/yr (38.4 -> 38.1 bps in one quarter on mix shift to CITs/SMAs/institutional).
base.margin_rationale: FY26 42.3% from guided opex growth 4-7%; then drifts 1.3pp lower over four years as fee compression outruns the expense program, stabilising at 41% (adjusted operating margin ~34.7%).
base.tax_rationale: Guided FY26 non-GAAP effective rate 24-27%; cash taxes paid FY25 $595.4M track the provision. 25% flat.

scenario_narratives.base: Active-to-passive keeps bleeding the equity mutual-fund franchise (H1-26 net outflows $20.2B, management guiding H2 flows 'meaningfully more challenging'), target-date (~33% of AUM, $622B) stays roughly flow-neutral-to-positive, and ETFs/SMAs/OHA alternatives grow but are too small to turn aggregate flows. Market appreciation roughly offsets outflows plus fee-rate decay, so revenue grows ~2% a year after a market-driven FY26, and the expense program holds adjusted operating margin in the mid-30s rather than defending the 36-37% of 2026. The dividend and buyback are funded comfortably from ~$2B of owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Flows turn: the ETF platform (~$30B, $4.4B Q2 inflows), SMAs and OHA's wealth-channel credit products (OFLEX, the Goldman private-markets fund) scale while equity outflows moderate as relative performance recovers; target-date keeps compounding with the DC market. Fee-rate decline slows as alternatives (higher fee) offset CIT mix shift, revenue grows 4-6% for five years, and operating leverage on a restructured cost base lifts adjusted EBITDA margin to ~45%, close to the pre-2022 run-rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: A ~20% equity drawdown in 2027 hits a business that is ~60% equity-beta through AUM, while net outflows accelerate (equity redemptions plus a recordkeeper or plan-sponsor default-option loss in target-date, the concentration risk flagged in the analysis). Revenue falls 10% and never recovers its trend as fee compression and passive share gains continue (-1%/yr), and costs prove sticky so adjusted EBITDA margin compresses to ~35%. Terminal growth zero: a melting active franchise, cash-generative but shrinking.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% house default) because the secular active-to-passive shift is a documented, multi-year headwind (FY25 net outflows $56.9B) and revenue is a direct claim on equity-market levels near record highs. Base 50%: consistent with five years of outflows offset by markets. Bull 25% (down from 35%) because it needs flows to turn positive and fee-rate decay to slow at the same time, which has not happened since 2021.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TROW is valued as a debt-free fee-stream operating business: adjusted operating income (excluding consolidated funds, deferred-comp marks and acquisition amortization) built up to adjusted EBITDA, SBC fully expensed, capex at ~3.6% of revenue, discounted at a 10% cost of equity. The ~$30/share of attributable cash and investments is added separately and all income on it is excluded from the flows. The market price sits close to a no-growth value of the fee stream plus the investment portfolio, i.e. it already discounts a slow melt; the debate is whether outflows and fee compression outrun market appreciation.
key_risks_to_valuation: Equity-market drawdown: revenue tracks AUM with roughly one-quarter lag, and costs are sticky in the short run
Net outflows accelerate (equity mutual funds, target-date recordkeeper/default-option losses)
Effective fee rate decline faster than the ~1-1.5%/yr assumed
OHA private-credit losses or valuation marks on the $751M affiliated-fund and seed exposure
Bridge relies on carrying values of seed/private-fund/UTI investments, not a realisation value net of tax
